sys-backup (NEW SYSTEM) — a pre-merge backup so a merge can never lose the code it replaced. Built drsamonline/backup (PUBLIC: backup.py + a reusable workflow + README + 17 tests) and drsamonline/dumps (the store). It snapshots a repo's tarball at the ref about to be replaced into <owner>__<repo>/<date-time>/<repo>.tar.gz, keeps the newest 100 per repo (deleting the oldest beyond), and creates dumps-2, dumps-3 ... when a dumps repo passes its size cap, so a full repo cannot block a backup. PROVEN: the first real dump is in drsamonline/dumps (ml-kit @ fbeb57d, 8947 B, read back byte-for-byte), and 17 unit tests pass; disabling rotation fails 4. Wired into forge via .github/workflows/backup.yml (on pull_request -> snapshots the BASE commit). TWO THINGS FOR THE OWNER: (1) add the BACKUP_TOKEN secret (contents:write on dumps, contents:read on the source) - without it the job SKIPS with a warning, it does not fail the PR and does not pretend it ran; (2) drsamonline/dumps is PRIVATE on purpose, because it will hold forge's private code - making it public would publish it.
